**1. MEMO.quote: 1.ADOPT — Status Quo / Null Option + mode-readiness rule. Retain static Astro; all three modes remain DEFER. Rule: a mode becomes considerable only when (a) a supplied feature artifact names a behavior static output cannot deliver, and (b) its bounded proof passes on the installed versions. Immediate adoption of any mode/design is DISMISSed as premature. Portability of HTTP is technically possible (I), not verified compatibility, and not product-justified.

1.ADOPT — Null + responsibility-placement readiness rule. No forms, auth, sessions, or private pages now; no intermediary choice. Rule (conditional): identity, credentials, and trust-boundary validation live in the backend; presentation hints may live in Astro; session persistence is persistence-domain and would trip the Q3 persistence re-gate; cookie/CSRF/CORS policy follows origin topology, which is unset.

1.ADOPT — Null + boundary/contract readiness rule. No API, shared package, generated client, or schema tool now. Rule: transport authority stays at the API boundary; internal Rust domain types never become frontend types by assumption; any future contract artifact must be generated or checked, not hand-synced; runtime validation, not compile-time types alone, guards the boundary.

1.ADOPT — Null + carried ownership + deployment-evidence readiness rule. Deployment invocation ownership stays with repository-level infrastructure (carried monorepo Q3 lock — not re-decided here). No host, adapter, proxy, CI, or backend runtime now.
